intended_object: The chain map C_•(Y, X; R) → C_•(Y', X'; R) between relative simplicial chain complexes that a morphism of pairs of simplicial sets (X ⊆ Y) → (X' ⊆ Y') induces. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The relative chain complex `P.chainComplex R` is defined as the value at `R` and `P` of the bifunctor `chainComplexFunctor`. That bifunctor is the cokernel of the natural map from the chain complex of `P.left` to the chain complex of `P.right`. So for each pair it gives the quotient complex C(Y)/C(X), the standard relative chain complex.

`chainComplexMap f R` is simply the action of the functor `(chainComplexFunctor C).obj R` on the morphism of pairs `f`. This is exactly the map induced on the quotients by the maps f_left and f_right. It is functorial by construction, and the library uses it to define `homologyMap` on relative homology.

The setting is natural. Coefficients lie in any preadditive category with coproducts (the usual case is Ab with ℤ), and pairs of simplicial sets are arbitrary monomorphisms. This is at least as general as the standard notion, so the definition is not too narrow. Mathlib has no other declaration for this object.
